description: Explore 35+ stunning hotel logos from luxury resorts to boutique stays. See what makes hospitality branding memorable and trustworthy.
body:
In the competitive world of hospitality, logos & branding play a crucial role in creating the hotel’s desired perception and identity.

As a logo designer with a keen eye for good branding, I’d like to review hotel logos to showcase how you can elevate your hotel’s brand identity.

Let’s explore some of the most impressive logos from renowned hotel brands and discover how their design principles effectively communicate in the hospitality industry.

1. Marriott

Marriott’s logo exemplifies a masterful blend of simplicity and sophistication, perfectly capturing the essence of this renowned hospitality brand.

Key features:

  • Abstract symbol formed by two intersecting “M” shapes
  • Bold, deep red color exuding warmth and luxury
  • Clean, modern sans-serif typeface for the wordmark
  • Balanced composition with symbol above text
  • Minimalist design that’s easily recognizable and scalable

The logo’s abstract “M” symbol, created by two intersecting shapes, cleverly represents the brand initial while also evoking images of mountain peaks or open doors — symbols of adventure and hospitality respectively. The deep red color choice conveys a sense of warmth, passion, and luxury, all key attributes in the hospitality industry.

The clean lines and geometric shapes of the symbol give the logo a contemporary feel, while also hinting at the precision and reliability Marriott is known for. The use of negative space within the symbol adds depth and interest, making the logo more memorable.

2. Sheraton

Sheraton’s logo presents a refined and elegant design that effectively communicates the brand’s long-standing heritage in the hospitality industry.

Key features:

  • Circular emblem featuring a stylized “S” at its center
  • Laurel wreath-like pattern surrounding the “S”, created by angled lines
  • Sophisticated gray color scheme
  • Clean, modern sans-serif typeface for the wordmark
  • Inclusion of establishment date “EST. 1937”
  • Balanced composition with emblem centered above text
  • Ample white space enhancing visual clarity

The logo’s focal point is the circular emblem, which cleverly incorporates a stylized “S” within a pattern reminiscent of a laurel wreath. This design choice not only represents the brand initial but also evokes associations with prestige and achievement, subtly positioning Sheraton as a leader in the hospitality sector.

The choice of a sophisticated gray color palette lends an air of timeless elegance to the logo. It’s a versatile choice that works well across various applications and conveys professionalism and refinement.

3. Holiday Inn

Holiday Inn’s logo embodies a fresh, inviting approach that effectively communicates the brand’s welcoming and accessible nature in the hospitality industry.

Key features:

  • Stylized “H” symbol with a playful, script-like quality
  • Vibrant green color scheme
  • Modern, custom-designed lowercase typeface for the wordmark
  • Slight rightward slant in both symbol and text, suggesting forward movement
  • Simple two-element composition (symbol and wordmark)
  • Ample white space enhancing visual appeal and readability

The stylized “H” symbol serves as an instantly recognizable brand identifier. Its script-like quality, with rounded edges and a fluid form, evokes a sense of friendliness and approachability. The vibrant green color is particularly noteworthy, often associated with freshness, growth, and renewal, aligning well with the concept of a refreshing stay or a new adventure.

The wordmark, set in a custom-designed lowercase typeface, complements the “H” symbol perfectly. The rounded, friendly letterforms reinforce the approachable nature of the brand. The use of lowercase letters further emphasizes a casual, welcoming atmosphere, in contrast to the more formal uppercase styles often seen in luxury hotel branding.

4. Conrad Hotels & Resorts

Conrad Hotels & Resorts’ logo embodies luxury and sophistication, perfectly aligning with the brand’s position in the high-end hospitality market.

Key features:

  • All-caps wordmark in a custom, modern serif typeface
  • “HOTELS & RESORTS” tagline in a smaller, sans-serif font
  • Gold color scheme conveying luxury and prestige
  • Clean, minimalist design with ample white space
  • Balanced composition with perfect alignment

The logo’s primary focus is the Conrad wordmark, set in a custom-designed modern serif typeface. The serifs are subtle and refined, adding a touch of elegance without appearing overly traditional. The use of all capital letters projects confidence and authority, while the generous spacing between letters enhances the sense of luxury and exclusivity.

The addition of “HOTELS & RESORTS” in a smaller, sans-serif font provides clarity about the brand’s offering while maintaining the overall elegance of the design. The gold color scheme is a classic choice for luxury brands, evoking associations with precious metals and high-end experiences.

The minimalist approach, with its ample white space, allows the logo to breathe and stand out, reinforcing the brand’s commitment to providing spacious, luxurious accommodations. Overall, Conrad’s logo successfully communicates a sense of modern luxury and sophisticated hospitality.

5. Radisson Hotels & Resorts

Radisson’s logo showcases a dynamic and contemporary design that effectively communicates the brand’s modern approach to hospitality.

Key features:

  • Script-style wordmark with a distinctive flowing “R”
  • Vibrant lime green underline accent
  • Addition of “HOTELS & RESORTS” in a clean sans-serif font
  • Black and green color combination for contrast and energy
  • Balanced composition with the accent drawing the eye across the logo

The logo’s standout feature is the script-style wordmark, particularly the flowing “R” that leads into the rest of the name. This creates a sense of movement and fluidity, potentially symbolizing the seamless experience Radisson aims to provide its guests. The lime green underline adds a pop of color and modernity to the otherwise classic black text.

The addition of “HOTELS & RESORTS” in a simple sans-serif font grounds the logo and clearly communicates the nature of the business. This dual-font approach allows Radisson to balance a touch of elegance with clear, straightforward information.

6. Accor

Accor’s logo presents a minimalist yet powerful design that effectively represents the group’s diverse portfolio of hospitality brands.

Key features:

  • Stylized “A” symbol resembling a bird or mountain peak
  • Gold color scheme conveying luxury and prestige
  • Clean, all-caps sans-serif typeface for the wordmark
  • Simple two-element composition (symbol and wordmark)
  • Ample white space for a clean, uncluttered look

The logo’s focal point is the abstract “A” symbol, which can be interpreted in multiple ways. It resembles a bird in flight, suggesting freedom and the joy of travel. Alternatively, it could be seen as a mountain peak, representing achievement and the heights of luxury. The gold color reinforces these associations with prestige and high-end experiences.

The wordmark, set in a clean, all-caps sans-serif font, provides a solid foundation for the more expressive symbol. This balance of abstract and concrete elements in the logo reflects Accor’s position as a parent company overseeing a variety of hotel brands, each with its own unique identity.

7. Hyatt

Hyatt’s logo exemplifies understated elegance and modernity, perfectly aligning with the brand’s upscale positioning in the hospitality market.

Key features:

  • Wordmark-centric design with a subtle graphic element
  • Custom-designed typeface with distinctive “A” characters
  • Curved line under the wordmark, suggesting a smile or horizon
  • Cool blue color scheme evoking trust and tranquility
  • Generous spacing between letters for a luxurious feel

The logo’s primary focus is the Hyatt wordmark, set in a custom-designed typeface. The most distinctive feature is the treatment of the “A” characters, which lack a horizontal bar and instead use negative space to create the letter shape. This unique touch adds visual interest and memorability to the logo.

The curved line beneath the wordmark serves multiple purposes. It can be interpreted as a welcoming smile, reinforcing the brand’s commitment to hospitality. Alternatively, it might represent a horizon line, evoking thoughts of travel and new experiences. The cool blue color scheme further enhances these associations, while also conveying a sense of calm and reliability.

8. The Ritz-Carlton

The Ritz-Carlton’s logo exudes timeless luxury and aristocratic heritage, perfectly encapsulating the brand’s position at the pinnacle of high-end hospitality.

Key features:

  • Heraldic lion and crown emblem
  • Classic serif typeface for the wordmark
  • Black and white color scheme for timeless elegance
  • Balanced composition with emblem centered above text
  • Use of negative space within the emblem for detail and depth

The logo’s centerpiece is the heraldic lion and crown emblem, a symbol deeply rooted in European nobility and luxury. The lion, often associated with strength and regality, wears a crown, further emphasizing the brand’s association with the highest levels of service and accommodation. The intricate details within the emblem, achieved through clever use of negative space, reward closer inspection and add to the logo’s sophisticated appeal.

The wordmark, set in a classic serif typeface, complements the emblem perfectly. The use of all capital letters and generous letter spacing adds to the sense of grandeur and exclusivity. The simple black and white color scheme ensures the logo remains elegant and timeless, capable of application across various media without losing its impact.

9. Hilton

Hilton’s logo presents a clever blend of traditional and modern design elements, effectively communicating the brand’s long-standing reputation and contemporary relevance.

Key features:

  • Stylized “H” monogram enclosed in an oval
  • Serif typeface for the wordmark, with a subtle modern twist
  • Navy blue color scheme conveying trust and professionalism
  • Balanced composition with monogram to the left of the wordmark
  • Use of negative space within the monogram to create a sense of movement

The logo’s focal point is the stylized “H” monogram, cleverly designed to incorporate two rectangular shapes that could represent hotel buildings or open doors. The use of negative space within the monogram creates a sense of movement or flow, possibly symbolizing the guest’s journey or the brand’s forward-thinking approach. The enclosing oval adds a touch of classic elegance and ensures the monogram stands out.

The wordmark, while using a serif typeface that nods to Hilton’s long history, has subtle modern touches that keep it feeling contemporary. The navy blue color scheme is a classic choice in the business world, conveying trustworthiness, stability, and professionalism — all key attributes for a global hotel chain.

Conclusion

The logos of these prominent hotel chains offer valuable lessons in creating lasting brand identities for the hospitality industry:

  1. Simplicity often leads to the most effective and memorable logos, as seen in the minimalist designs of Marriott and Accor.
  2. Color choices play a crucial role in conveying brand personality, from Hilton’s professional navy to Conrad’s luxurious gold.
  3. Symbols and monograms can powerfully represent brand values and heritage, as demonstrated by Sheraton’s laurel wreath and The Ritz-Carlton’s heraldic emblem.
  4. Typography is key in expressing brand character, from Radisson’s dynamic script to Conrad’s refined serif font.
  5. Negative space can be used creatively to add depth and meaning, as seen in the Hilton monogram.
  6. Balancing traditional elements with modern design keeps long-standing brands relevant, exemplified by Sheraton and Hyatt.
  7. Abstract designs can effectively communicate complex brand identities, as shown by Marriott’s intersecting shapes and Accor’s multifaceted symbol.

When designing a logo for the hospitality industry, consider how you can distill your brand’s unique approach, values, and guest experience into a simple, memorable mark. Remember that your logo will be used across various applications, from building signage to mobile apps, so versatility and scalability are crucial.
